prompts.title: Azure Well-Architected review
prompts.description: Get a structured review of an Azure architecture against the five Well-Architected pillars, with prioritized fixes.

prompts.title: Bicep module generator
prompts.description: Generate a clean, parameterized and secure-by-default Bicep module for any Azure resource.
prompts.body:
Act as an Azure infrastructure-as-code expert. Write a production-ready Bicep module that deploys {{Azure resource}}.

Requirements:
- Target API version: the latest stable one you know of. Say which one you used.
- Parameters with @description, sensible defaults and @allowed values where relevant.
- Secure by default: private networking when the service supports it, TLS 1.2 minimum, managed identity, public network access disabled, diagnostic settings sent to a Log Analytics workspace passed as a parameter.
- Naming follows this convention: {{Naming convention}}
- Tags passed as an object parameter.
- Outputs: resource ID, name and any endpoint a consumer would need.

Follow the Azure Verified Modules (AVM) style. After the code, give a short example of how to call the module from a main.bicep file, and list the security choices you made.

prompts.title: Improve my prompt
prompts.description: A meta-prompt that rewrites your prompt to be clearer, more specific and more reliable.
prompts.body:
You are a prompt engineering expert. Improve the prompt below so that an LLM gives a more accurate, useful and consistent answer.

My prompt:
"""
{{Your prompt}}
"""

Goal of the prompt: {{What you want to get}}

Steps:
1. Diagnose the prompt in a few bullets: ambiguity, missing context, missing output format, missing constraints.
2. Ask me up to 3 questions only if they would change the result a lot.
3. Write the improved prompt. Include a role, context, the task, constraints, the expected output format and an example if useful. Mark anything I must fill in as a placeholder wrapped in double curly braces.
4. Explain in 3 bullets what you changed and why.

prompts.title: KQL query builder
prompts.description: Turn a plain-language question into a commented KQL query for Log Analytics, Microsoft Sentinel or Azure Resource Graph.
variables: Target (Log Analytics, Sentinel or Resource Graph)
prompts.body:
You are a Kusto Query Language (KQL) expert. Write a query for {{Target (Log Analytics, Sentinel or Resource Graph)}} that answers this question:

"{{Your question}}"

Known tables or columns (optional): {{Tables or columns}}

Requirements:
- Filter on time early (default: the last 24 hours) and project only the useful columns.
- Comment each step with //.
- Prefer summarize and render for anything that is a trend.
- If a table name is a guess, say so and suggest how to check it.

After the query, explain in three bullet points how it works and one way to turn it into an alert rule.

prompts.title: Funko pop
prompts.description: Design a personalized collectible figure and matching limited-edition box, with custom appearance, clothes, accessories and packaging.
variables: Eyes and eyelashes (for example, large dark eyes with long eyelashes)
Facial hair (for example, a short white beard or none)
Top (for example, a black henley T-shirt)
Outerwear (for example, a grey pullover hoodie)
Clothing logo or text (for example, Azure in blue)
Held accessory (for example, a Surface laptop)
Box colors (for example, grey and blue)
Background (for example, a clean white background)
prompts.body:
Create a high-quality 3D render of a Funko Pop-style collectible figure with the following personalized details:

- Character name: {{Character name (for example, Ben)}}.
- Gender or presentation: {{Gender or presentation (for example, male)}}.
- Facial expression: {{Facial expression (for example, smiling)}}.
- Eyes and eyelashes: {{Eyes and eyelashes (for example, large dark eyes with long eyelashes)}}.
- Hair: {{Hair (for example, short black hair)}}.
- Facial hair: {{Facial hair (for example, a short white beard or none)}}.
- Top: {{Top (for example, a black henley T-shirt)}}.
- Outerwear: {{Outerwear (for example, a grey pullover hoodie)}}.
- Clothing logo or text: {{Clothing logo or text (for example, Azure in blue)}}.
- Bottoms: {{Bottoms (for example, blue jeans)}}.
- Shoes: {{Shoes (for example, black moccasins)}}.
- Socks: {{Socks (for example, black socks)}}.
- Held accessory: {{Held accessory (for example, a Surface laptop)}}.

Display two matching copies of the character in the same scene: one inside its limited-edition collectible box and one standing outside, next to the box. Both figures must have the same appearance, outfit and accessory.

Packaging:
- Box colors: {{Box colors (for example, grey and blue)}}.
- Front-of-box text: "{{Front-of-box text (for example, Boss)}}".
- Print "{{Character name (for example, Ben)}}" as the character name on the packaging.
- Include a large transparent front window, allowing a clear view of the figure inside.
- Use clean, legible typography and a polished limited-edition packaging design.

Composition and rendering:
- Background: {{Background (for example, a clean white background)}}.
- Use a three-quarter product view with both the boxed and unboxed figures fully visible.
- Give the figure an oversized head, a small body, stylized proportions and a smooth vinyl finish.
- Use soft studio lighting, realistic materials, subtle shadows and a crisp, professional 3D product-render aesthetic.
- Reproduce the requested clothing text, character name and box text accurately. Do not add unrelated text or accessories.

prompts.title: My sweet house
prompts.description: Analyze house photos into a detailed house sheet, then create a faithful isometric miniature diorama after the analysis has been confirmed.
prompts.models: AI assistant with image analysis and image generation
prompts.body:
Use the attached house photos as the reference. Work in two stages: complete Stage 1 only, then wait for my answers to any questions and my explicit approval before starting Stage 2.

## Stage 1: Analyze the house

Analyze the attached photos of my house. Do NOT generate any image yet. Write a precise, numbered HOUSE SHEET with:

1. Overall shape and footprint, number of storeys, attached buildings.
2. Roof: type, number of slopes, material, color, chimneys, skylights.
3. Walls: materials and colors per facade.
4. For EACH visible facade: number and position of windows (left to right, per floor), doors, shutters type (roller / swing / none), their color.
5. Garage: number of doors, door type (sectional / roller / swing), position.
6. Plot: gate type (sliding / swing / none), fences, low walls, driveway, paths, terrace, pool, pergola, awning, garden elements, trees.
7. Every exterior light fixture you can see and its exact position.
8. Anything unclear or not visible in the photos: list it as a question.

## Stage 2: Generate the diorama after approval

Transform the attached photo of my house into a highly detailed 3D isometric miniature diorama.

FIDELITY: keep the exact architecture, proportions, roof shape, number and position of windows, doors and garage doors, and the surrounding elements (driveway, garden, fences, trees). Do not add or remove any building element.

CAMERA: true isometric view, front three-quarter angle, the whole property visible and centered, nothing cropped, generous empty margin around the model.

STYLE: clean stylized 3D render, soft global illumination, smooth matte materials, subtle ambient occlusion, premium architectural model look.

LIGHTING: bright sunny day, soft shadows. All exterior and interior lights OFF. All garage doors, gates and shutters CLOSED.

BACKGROUND: plain uniform dark background (#1C1C1C), no sky, no horizon. The diorama sits on a thin square ground base with clean edges.

NO text, NO labels, NO people, NO cars, NO watermark. Landscape 16:9, maximum resolution.

prompts.title: PowerPoint deck creation
prompts.description: Create complete French and US English PowerPoint decks with a dark developer-style design, editable visuals, sources and slide-by-slide quality checks.
prompts.models: AI assistant with file generation, code execution, web search and image generation
variables: Audience (for example, beginners, decision-makers or developers)
Goal (for example, explain the basics, persuade or train)
prompts.body:
## 1. The request

Create a PowerPoint presentation (.pptx) about **{{Topic}}**.

- **Audience**: {{Audience (for example, beginners, decision-makers or developers)}}.
- **Goal**: {{Goal (for example, explain the basics, persuade or train)}}.
- **Languages**: produce **two separate, complete decks**, one in **French** (`{{Deck name}}-FR.pptx`) and one in **US English** (`{{Deck name}}-EN.pptx`). Each deck is 100% in a single language. Write the two versions separately rather than translating word for word. Only product names and commands stay as they are.
- **Author** on the title slide and the closing slide: {{Author full name}} · {{Company}} · {{Month Year}}.
- **Sections I want**: {{Sections to cover}}, plus anything else you think is relevant.

## 2. Tone and language

- Write for beginners: short sentences, everyday words, no unexplained jargon.
- Explain every technical concept with **an everyday analogy**. Examples: "an LLM is like your phone keyboard, only far more powerful", "the instructions file is the note you leave for the babysitter", "a GPU is a whole kitchen crew working at once".
- Prefer **concrete examples without code**. Show code only when it is essential, and always inside a "code editor" card.
- Use plain, meaningful slide titles ("Asking the right way" rather than "Prompt engineering").
- Use the tools' **exact terminology** and check technical accuracy: command names, retired features, and so on.

## 3. Visual design (follow it strictly)

**Format**: 16:9 widescreen (13.33 × 7.5 inches), generated with code (pptxgenjs). Margins of 0.7 inch.

**Dark "developer-style" background on every slide**:

| Role | Color |
| --- | --- |
| Content slide background | `#0D1117` |
| Title, transition and closing slide background | `#010409` |
| Cards | `#161B22` (highlighted cards: `#1C2230`) |
| Borders | `#30363D` |
| Main text | `#E6EDF3` |
| Secondary text | `#9AA4B2` |
| Accents | violet `#A371F7` · blue `#58A6FF` · green `#3FB950` · amber `#E3B341` · pink `#F778BA` · cyan `#39C5CF` |

**Typography**:

- Titles and body text: **Segoe UI**.
- "Code" elements (kickers, labels, numbers): **Consolas**.
- Sizes: slide title 30 pt bold; intro line 14–15 pt in gray; body text 11–14 pt; sources 8.5–10 pt, gray italic.

**The visual motif, repeated on every slide**:

- A **code-style kicker** above the title, in the section's accent color, formatted like `// 02 · understand ai`.
- The title, then a one-line gray intro sentence.
- **Rounded cards** (0.11-inch radius) with a thin border, colored when the item is highlighted.
- **Icons in rounded square chips**, with a `#1C2230` fill and a border in the accent color. Icons come from react-icons and are converted to PNG in their real color, never black.
- A **takeaway bar** at the bottom of the slide: a bold colored keyword ("Key point", "In practice", "Tip"), then a dash and one sentence.
- **"Code editor" cards** for code: `#010409` background, three dots (pink, amber, green) at the top, Consolas font.

**Varied layouts.** Never use the same layout twice in a row. Alternate between:

- grids of 2 to 6 cards;
- side-by-side comparison columns ("Avoid / Better", "Without / With");
- comparison tables with one column highlighted by a badge ("our topic");
- step timelines linked by chevrons;
- ring diagrams or nested-box diagrams;
- big numbers (30–34 pt) with their source;
- a ranking podium;
- gauges and progress bars drawn with shapes, never a native chart object or a picture of a chart.

**Avoid**:

- decorative lines under titles and full-width colored bands;
- centered text in paragraphs;
- text-only slides;
- emojis.

## 4. Images

- **Title slide**: the product's official logo if it exists among the brand icons (react-icons/si), otherwise a simple icon.
- **Section and appendix transition slides**: an AI-generated illustration, in a round medallion on the right of the slide.
- Keep **the same style for every image** by repeating this description word for word in each image request:*glowing holographic neon illustration made of fine light lines and luminous particles, [section color] light with soft bloom, futuristic tech aesthetic. Isolated subject centered on a transparent background, no text, no letters, no logos.*
- An image in this style can also illustrate a key slide, for example a glowing brain to talk about memory.
- Never use generated images for diagrams, charts or text: build those as editable PowerPoint shapes.

## 5. Deck structure

1. **Title**: code kicker, large title, colored subtitle, one-line hook. On the right, a panel with the logo and 3 "what it does" items.
2. **Agenda by parts**: 4 to 5 colored cards (Part 1 to 4, then "Wrapping up"), each listing its topics, with an "Appendix" strip at the bottom.
3. **Words to know**: a glossary of 8 terms, each defined in one simple sentence.
4. **A transition slide before each part**: a large subtle number, "// part N of 4", the title, the list of topics, a 4-segment progress bar and an illustration in a round medallion.
5. **The content**, organized in parts: discover, understand, use, use well.
6. **Interactive slides**: a "Your turn" workshop (a vague request, the questions to ask, a precise version), and a "True or false?" quiz over 2 slides (the questions, then the answers with a TRUE or FALSE badge and an explanation).
7. **Wrapping up**: "What's next?" (trends), frequently asked questions, key takeaways, then a "Thank you / Questions?" slide.
8. **"Going further" appendix**: the detailed reference slides and the resources (clickable links).

Aim for about **30 to 35 presentation slides**, plus the appendix.

## 6. Accuracy and sources

- **Search the web** for up-to-date information (products, prices, figures, rankings) before writing. Never include a number without a source.
- Cite the **source at the bottom of the slide** (name, date), in small gray italics, for every figure, study, price or ranking.
- For anything that changes fast (models, prices, rankings), add a note such as "List as of [date]".
- If I provide an article, rephrase it in your own words without copying the text, and credit its author.

## 7. Quality check before delivery

- Render each deck to images and **check every slide**: no text overflowing or overlapping, margins of at least 0.5 inch, good contrast, no word broken at the end of a line.
- Check that each deck is entirely in its own language (« » quotes and decimal commas in French, " " quotes and decimal points in English).
- Fix any issues, then check the corrected slides a second time.
- Deliver both .pptx files and summarize the deck's content in a few lines.

prompts.title: Azure cost optimization plan
prompts.description: Analyze an Azure cost export and get a prioritized FinOps action plan with estimated savings.
variables: Context (production or not, working hours, growth)
prompts.body:
Act as an Azure FinOps practitioner. Here is a summary of my monthly Azure spend (service, resource, SKU, cost, usage):

{{Cost data}}

Environment context: {{Context (production or not, working hours, growth)}}

Produce:
1. The top cost drivers and whether each looks normal.
2. Quick wins (rightsizing, shutting down idle resources, deleting orphaned disks and IPs, cheaper storage tiers).
3. Commitment options (Reservations, Savings Plan, Azure Hybrid Benefit) with the break-even reasoning.
4. Architecture changes worth considering for the long term.
5. A table of actions with estimated monthly savings, effort and risk.

State your assumptions clearly. Do not recommend anything that would reduce production reliability without flagging it.

prompts.title: Blameless incident postmortem
prompts.description: Turn raw incident notes into a clear, blameless postmortem with a timeline, root cause and follow-up actions.
prompts.body:
You are an experienced SRE. Write a blameless postmortem from the raw notes below.

Raw notes, chat logs and timestamps:
{{Incident notes}}

Use this structure:
1. Summary (3 sentences: what happened, impact, how it was fixed)
2. Impact (users, services, duration, SLA or SLO consumed)
3. Timeline in UTC as a table (time, event, source)
4. Root cause, using the "5 whys" method
5. What went well and what went wrong
6. Action items as a table (action, owner role, priority, type: prevent, detect or mitigate)

Stay factual and blameless: describe systems and processes, never people. Mark clearly any point you had to assume.

prompts.title: Convert Terraform to Bicep
prompts.description: Translate Terraform (azurerm) code into equivalent, idiomatic Bicep and flag what does not map one to one.
prompts.body:
Convert the following Terraform code that uses the azurerm provider into idiomatic Bicep.

```hcl
{{Terraform code}}
```

Rules:
- Map each azurerm resource to its Microsoft.* resource type and a stable API version.
- Turn variables into Bicep parameters (keep descriptions and defaults) and locals into variables.
- Use symbolic references instead of hard-coded resource IDs, and existing resources where Terraform used data sources.
- Replace count and for_each with Bicep loops.

Then add a section named "Not a 1:1 mapping" that lists anything that behaves differently (state, lifecycle blocks, provider-only features) and how to handle it.

prompts.title: GitHub Actions workflow
prompts.description: Generate a secure GitHub Actions workflow with OIDC to Azure, least-privilege permissions and caching.

prompts.title: LinkedIn post from an article
prompts.description: Turn a technical article or release note into an engaging, non-cringe LinkedIn post.
variables: Audience (for example, Azure architects, developers, IT managers)
prompts.body:
Write a LinkedIn post in {{Output language}} based on the content below.

{{Article text or link summary}}

Audience: {{Audience (for example, Azure architects, developers, IT managers)}}

Guidelines:
- First line: a hook under 15 words that makes people click "see more", with no clickbait.
- 3 to 5 short paragraphs or bullets with the key takeaways and why they matter in practice.
- One personal insight or opinion, written in the first person.
- End with an open question to invite comments.
- At most 3 hashtags and 2 emoji. No buzzwords like "game changer" or "revolutionize".
- Under 1,300 characters.

Then give 2 alternative hooks.

prompts.title: Meeting notes to action items
prompts.description: Turn a messy transcript or notes into a crisp summary, decisions and an owner-based action list.
prompts.body:
Here are the notes or the transcript of a meeting about {{Meeting topic}}:

{{Notes or transcript}}

Write, in {{Output language}}:
1. A 5-line executive summary.
2. The decisions made (one bullet each).
3. A table of action items: action, owner, due date (write "TBD" when unknown).
4. Open questions and risks.
5. A short follow-up email I can send to attendees.

Do not invent decisions or owners that are not in the notes.

prompts.title: Thorough code review
prompts.description: Ask for a senior-level code review focused on bugs, security and maintainability, not style nitpicks.
prompts.body:
Act as a senior {{Language}} engineer doing a code review. Review the code below.

```
{{Code to review}}
```

Focus on, in this order:
1. Bugs and logic errors (edge cases, null handling, concurrency, off-by-one errors).
2. Security issues (injection, secrets, authorization, unsafe deserialization).
3. Performance problems that matter at scale.
4. Maintainability: naming, duplication, overly complex functions.

Ignore pure formatting and style preferences. For each finding, give the line or snippet, why it is a problem, a severity and a suggested fix as code. If the code is good, say so briefly instead of inventing problems.
